target_customer: SaaS companies needing low touch bookkeeping
problem: SaaS startups pay 300 to 1000 dollars a month for bookkeepers; Sway used machine learning and payment integrations to automate transaction categorization for a 99 dollar flat fee.
business_model: B2B SaaS flat monthly fee (99 dollars) with bookkeeper review

founders.name: Ashwin Kumar
education: UCLA (met co-founder there per YC launch post; degree not stated)
founders.background_notes: YC page says he later built AI products at Voxel Labs and was previously in product at Stripe; the timing relative to Sway is not stated.

founders.name: Catherine Jue
education: UCLA (met co-founder there per YC launch post; degree not stated)
founders.background_notes: YC launch post says she studied machine learning after reconciling her father's QuickBooks books; later co-founded and ran Kernel.

competitors.name: QuickBooks
competitors.what: Incumbent small business accounting software that Sway integrated with and automated around

technical_complexity.rationale: ML categorization of receipts and transactions (about 90 percent accurate per YC post) with payment and accounting integrations and human review.

defensibility.rationale: Proprietary models could improve with data but accounting vendors and bookkeeping services could replicate.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: The YC post says accounting software companies were too large to ship quickly; no acquisition found.

market_need_then: YC post cites bookkeepers at 300 to 1000 dollars a month versus Sway's 99 dollars; VentureBeat reported 10 pilot companies.

brand_strength.rationale: Product Hunt launches and VentureBeat coverage in 2016, a Slack investment, but several other companies share the Sway name.

pivots.why: VentureBeat says the bot grew from balances and transaction history into fuller accounting

outcome_analysis: Sway Finance began as a Slack finance bot, expanded into automated SaaS bookkeeping, got a Slack investment and a VentureBeat write up in 2016, and is now listed inactive. No shutdown announcement or cause was found; the founders went on to Voxel Labs and Kernel, so the cause is not public and failure factors are empty.
notes: Dealroom seed (125K at 2.0M valuation) is a single garbled database entry and is undated. The Slack investment is known only from an article title; amount and date not seen. YC launch post is undated in what I saw, so the QuickBooks competitor source_date is the batch year only. Phenomenon Studio branding case may describe a different company named Sway Finance. No company website listed.
